answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The spiral multiplier is published, charged in willow, and copper lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4469 identities would post 2128 proofs and burn roughly 86 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
